source_text: Denique ubi iam et familiaris populus allegi deo coepit et restitutio hominis imbui potuit, tunc leges disciplinaeque omnes impositae, etiam quae decerperent uictum, ademptis quibusdam ueluti immundis, quo facilius aliquando ieiunia toleraret homo perpetua in quibusdam abstinentia usus. nam et primus populus primi hominis resculpserat crimen pronior uentri quam deo deprehensus, cum de duritia Aegyptiae seruitutis ualida manu dei et sublimi brachio ereptus dominus eius uisus est, terrae lacte et melle mananti destinatus, statim autem solitudinis incopiosae circumspectu scandalizatus, saturitatis Aegyptiae detrimenta suspirans in Moysen et Aaron mussitauit: utinam obiissemus percussi a domino in terra Aegypti, quando super ollas carnium sedebamus et panes in plenitudinem comedebamus. quomodo eduxisti nos in haec deserta ad interficiendam synagogam istam fame? eadem uentris praelatione deploraturus erat eosdem duces suos et dei arbitros, quos desiderio carnis et recordatu Aegyptiarum copiarum exacerbabat. quis nos uescet carne? uenerunt in mentem nobis pisces quos in Aegypto edebamus gratis, et cucumeres et pepones et porri et cepe et allia. at nunc anima nostra arida, nihil nisi manna uident oculi nostri. ita et illis xerophagiae panis angelici displicebant, allium potius et cepe quam caelum fragrare malebant. et ideo tam ingratis gratiora et esculentiora quaeque detracta sunt, puniendae simul gulae et exercendae continentiae causa, ut illa damnaretur, ista erudiretur.
thought_title: Israel's food discipline and the belly's complaint
orientation: Tertullian is showing that God imposed food restrictions on Israel so that, practiced in abstinence, they could more easily endure fasting, but the people preferred their bellies to God.
pass_a_gloss: Then, when a people already belonging to God began to be chosen and the restoration of man could be instructed, then all laws and disciplines were imposed, even those which would cut back food, with certain things removed as unclean, so that man might more easily endure fasts at some time, having been practiced in perpetual abstinence from certain things. For the first people had also re-engraved the crime of the first man, being found more inclined to the belly than to God, when, having been snatched from the harshness of Egyptian slavery by the strong hand of God and the uplifted arm, its Lord was seen, destined for a land flowing with milk and honey, but immediately scandalized by the sight of the barren wilderness, sighing for the losses of Egyptian fullness, it muttered against Moses and Aaron: 'Would that we had died struck by the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat over pots of meat and ate bread to fullness. Why have you led us out into these deserts to kill this assembly by hunger?' By the same preference for the belly it was going to deplore those same leaders of its own and judges of God, whom it exasperated by desire for meat and recollection of Egyptian abundance. 'Who will feed us meat? There came into our mind the fish which we ate in Egypt for free, and cucumbers and melons and leeks and onions and garlic. But now our soul is dry, our eyes see nothing except manna.' Thus even to them the dry-food fasts of angelic bread were displeasing; they preferred garlic and onion to smell fragrant rather than heaven. And therefore from such ungrateful people every more pleasing and more edible thing was taken away, for the sake of punishing gluttony and training self-control at the same time, so that the former might be condemned, the latter instructed.

choices.english: a people already belonging to God
choices.why: familiaris means belonging to the household/family; 'already belonging to God' captures the covenant relationship without importing 'chosen people' cliché
restitutio is restoration/renewal; 'man' keeps the generic singular of the Latin
imbuere means to imbue/instruct in first principles; 'instructed' fits the pedagogical context of laws being imposed
decerpere is literally to pluck off; 'cut back' conveys restriction of diet
resculpere is to carve again; 're-engraved' preserves the image of imprinting Adam's sin anew

choices.english: the dry-food fasts of angelic bread
choices.why: xerophagiae is the glossary term 'dry-food fasts'; 'angelic bread' renders panis angelici literally, referring to manna
rejected: the dry diet of angelic bread
the bread-and-water fast of angelic bread

pass_b_english: Then, when a people already belonging to God began to be chosen and the restoration of man could be renewed, all the laws and disciplines were imposed, including those that would cut back food, with certain things removed as unclean, so that man might more easily endure fasting at times, having become accustomed to permanent abstinence from some foods. For the first people had re-engraved the crime of the first man, caught as more inclined to the belly than to God. When he was rescued from the harshness of Egyptian slavery by the mighty hand of God and the uplifted arm, and his Lord was seen, destined for a land flowing with milk and honey, he was immediately scandalized by the sight of the barren wilderness. Sighing over the loss of Egyptian fullness, he muttered against Moses and Aaron: "If only we had died struck down by the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat over pots of meat and ate bread to the full. Why have you led us out into this desert to kill this whole assembly with hunger?" (Exodus 16:3). He was going to lament the same leaders and arbiters of God with the same preference for the belly, whom he exasperated with his craving for meat and his recollection of Egyptian abundance. "Who will feed us meat? We remember the fish we ate in Egypt for free, and the cucumbers and melons and leeks and onions and garlic. But now our soul is dry; our eyes see nothing but manna" (Numbers 11:4-6). So even for them the angelic bread of manna was displeasing; they preferred the fragrance of garlic and onion to heaven. And therefore, from such ungrateful people, the more pleasing and delicious foods were taken away, both to punish gluttony and to train self-control, so that the one might be condemned and the other instructed.

problems.fix: the restoration of man could be renewed

edits.old: the restoration of man could be instructed
edits.new: the restoration of man could be renewed

fixed: Changed 'instructed' to 'renewed' for 'imbui potuit', which means 'could be imbued/renewed', not 'instructed'.

problems.quote: the dry-food fasts of angelic bread
problems.why: Manna is called angelic bread; calling it a 'dry-food fast' is confusing since they ate it, just disliked it.
problems.fix: Rewrite: 'even the angelic bread of manna was displeasing to them.'

variants.text: the dry-food fasts of angelic bread

edits.old: So even for them the dry-food fasts of angelic bread were displeasing; they preferred the fragrance of garlic and onion to heaven.
edits.new: So even for them the angelic bread of manna was displeasing; they preferred the fragrance of garlic and onion to heaven.

fixed: The source says 'ita et illis xerophagiae panis angelici displicebant' — the manna (angelic bread) displeased them; calling it 'dry-food fasts' misstates the source, since they ate it but disliked it. Changed to 'the angelic bread of manna was displeasing.'

last_rejected.quote: re-engraved the crime of the first man
last_rejected.source_quote: resculpserat crimen pronior ventri quam deo
last_rejected.why: Latin means ‘rebuked/reproached the crime’, not ‘re‑engraved’; changes meaning of how the first people dealt with Adam’s sin.
last_rejected.fix: rebuked the crime of the first man
last_rejected.ruling: resculpserat literally means 're-engraved'; 'rebuked' is unsupported. Image of re-inscribing Adam's crime fits Tertullian's rhetorical style.
